item.title: Islami Bank to increase authorised capital by Tk 80 billion
item.description:
Islami Bank has decided to increase its authorised capital from Tk 20 billion to Tk 100 billion. The decision was taken at a meeting of the bank’s board of directors held on 4 November.

As a listed company, the bank informed its shareholders of the decision through the stock exchanges yesterday, Thursday.

Speaking on condition of anonymity about the decision to increase the bank's capital, a senior bank official told Prothom Alo, “The bank has fallen into a capital crisis due to irregularities by the S Alam Group. We are therefore trying to bring a foreign strategic investor on board by increasing the authorised capital. The recommendation to raise the capital came from Bangladesh Bank. We hope Bangladesh Bank will approve our decision.”

S Alam out, Al-Arafah Islami Bank now under KDS' control

According to the announcement made by Islami Bank to the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), the decision to increase authorised capital will be implemented through necessary amendments to the bank’s memorandum of association.

It will take effect subject to approval from Bangladesh Bank and other regulatory authorities, as well as final approval by shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting.

It is learnt that Islami Bank Bangladesh posted a net loss of Tk 33.03 billion after tax in the first nine months (January-September) of the current calendar year.

S Alam group laundered Tk 2.25 trillion: BFIU report

In contrast, the bank had earned a profit of around Tk 790 million in the first nine months of the previous year. The bank also incurred a loss of Tk 19.76 billion in the first quarter (July-September) of the 2026-27 fiscal year.

According to the bank’s data, its asset value has fallen by nearly half due to the huge losses. As of 30 September, the bank’s net asset value (NAV) stood at Tk 35.84 billion, compared with Tk 69.63 billion during the same period last year. As a result, its net asset value per share has also declined.

Islami Bank, which is facing a financial crisis, has been unable to pay any dividends to its shareholders since 2023. As a result, the bank is now classified in the Z category as a low-grade company on the stock market.

A mysterious visit by S Alam to Islami Bank

The S Alam Group of Chattogram took control of Islami Bank in 2017. Since then, the group has withdrawn nearly Tk 1 trillion from the bank through loans taken in its own name and under other names. All of those loans have now become defaulted.

The S Alam Group lost control of the bank after the Awami League government was ousted in the mass uprising on 5 August 2024. During the interim government’s tenure, independent directors were given responsibility for running the bank. Bangladesh Bank has now taken over its management.

item.description:
The Bangladesh Parliamentary Caucus on Migration, Rights and Development was formally inaugurated on Wednesday, 4 November 2026 at The Westin Dhaka, bringing together parliamentarians, government representatives, development partners and international organizations, CSOs, media, trade union, private sector and migration experts to strengthen migration governance and protect the rights of Bangladeshi migrant workers, reports a press release.

The programme was attended by the speaker of parliament Hafiz Uddin Ahmad, as chief guest, deputy speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal, as special guest, and state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam with state minister for expatriates’ welfare and overseas employment Md Nurul Haque as guests of honour. The event was chaired by caucus chairperson ABM Mosharraf Hossain.

Diversification of migration destination: Focusing on talent partnership programme

Mahmuda Habiba, secretary general of the caucus delivered her opening speech and introduced the parliamentary caucus executive and general members. Syed Saiful Haque, chairman, WARBE DF, secretariat of the parliamentary caucus delivered his welcome speech.

In his address, Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad said, “Migration is not just about remittances sent from abroad; it is also about the rights, dignity and security of our people.” Highlighting the hardships faced by migrant workers, particularly women, he stressed the need for stronger enforcement of migration laws and better protection in destination countries. He also called for Bangladesh to be developed as a migration destination and urged parliamentarians to use the caucus as a platform to facilitate overseas employment and monitor the implementation of migration laws at the grassroots.

Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal highlighted the contribution of migrant workers to the national economy, stating, “The remittances sent by migrant workers are a driving force of our economy.” He also stressed the need for diplomatic missions to take stronger measures to protect migrant workers' rights and address exploitation abroad.

State minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam and state minister for expatriates’ welfare and overseas employment Md Nurul Haque highlighted the importance of government initiatives and institutional coordination in addressing migration-related challenges, and ensuring better services and protection for migrant workers.

The panel discussion brought attention to persistent challenges in the migration sector, including high recruitment costs, unregulated intermediaries, human trafficking and gaps in the implementation of existing policies. Panelists also emphasised the importance of fair recruitment, psychosocial and socioeconomic protection, and stronger coordination between the ministries of foreign affairs and home affairs to address human trafficking.

Female worker migration rises, but remains dependent on two countries

At the event solidarity statements were delivered by Kazi Faisal Bin Seraj, country representative, The Asia Foundation; James Goldman, deputy high commissioner and development director to Bangladesh, British High Commission, Dhaka; Max Tuñón, country director, International Labour Organization (ILO) in Bangladesh; Laura Tomm Bonde, chief of mission, International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Bangladesh; Diepak Elmer, deputy head of mission / head of cooperation, Embassy of Switzerland in Bangladesh; Antonio Alessandro, ambassador, Embassy of Italy in Dhaka; and Ambassador Nahida Sobhan, rector, Foreign Service Academy, Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The newly inaugurated all-party Caucus will serve as a dedicated parliamentary platform to advance evidence-based policy reform, strengthen oversight and ensure that the concerns of migrant workers are reflected in national decision-making. It will also promote stronger coordination among parliamentarians, government institutions, civil society and development partners.

The inauguration calls for collective commitment and coordinated action to ensure safe, orderly and regular migration, fair recruitment practices and the protection of the rights and dignity of Bangladeshi migrant workers. The programme was organised by the Caucus Secretariat, WARBE Development Foundation, with support from the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) and The Asia Foundation.

item.title: Jack Dorsey’s Block is cutting jobs again. Here’s what makes these layoffs different
item.description:
Jack Dorsey’s fintech company, Block, began a second round of layoffs on Wednesday, months after cutting more than 4,000 jobs in February. The company has not said how many employees are affected at this time. 

The cuts hit the Customer Ops, Risk Ops, and Learning & Content Operations teams supporting Cash App, Block’s consumer financial services app, and Square, its tool for sellers. According to Business Insider, those teams will be “reducing the number of roles, changing some responsibilities, and shifting some reporting lines.” 

Affected employees are expected to receive a “separation package and transition support, similar to those affected in February 2026.” Block has not detailed the new terms. In February, laid-off employees received 20 weeks of severance or more, depending on their tenure, equity vested until the end of May, six months of healthcare, any corporate devices, and an extra $5,000. 

Block did not respond to Fast Company’s request for comment as of publication. 

The layoffs came one day after Block reported its third-quarter results on Tuesday. The company said it raised its 2026 gross profit forecast to $12.63 billion, up from its initial $12.51 billion estimate. It also projected fourth-quarter gross profit of $3.32 billion. 

Block hasn’t explained what drove this round of layoffs. Earlier this year, Dorsey announced that the February layoffs were not because of financial issues, but because of “intelligence tools,” like AI.

“A significantly smaller team, using the tools we’re building, can do more and do it better,” Dorsey wrote on X. “Intelligence tool capabilities are compounding faster every week.”

“We see an opportunity to move faster with smaller, highly talented teams using AI to automate more work,” Block CFO Amrita Ahuja said. 

Block is also continuing to build its own AI products. The company recently released Dessa, a speech-to-speech AI voice model trained on the recording of real human conversations.

item.title: Nintendo reports profit is up 11%, but sales slipped for the first half of the fiscal year
item.description:
Japanese video-game maker Nintendo reported Thursday an 11% improvement in its net profit in the first half of the fiscal year, although its sales declined during that period.

Kyoto-based Nintendo Co.’s April-September profit rose to 220.9 billion yen ($1.4 billion) from nearly 199 billion yen in the same period a year earlier. Sales during the six months slipped 12% to 966 billion yen.

Nintendo, which makes Pokemon, Super Mario and Legend of Zelda games, sold 1.27 million Switch game consoles during the six months, and 6.49 million of its Switch 2 machines, the company said.

In game software, “Star Fox” and “Splatoon Raiders,” released during that period, sold briskly, while earlier releases like “Mario Kart World” were still in demand, it said.

Nintendo’s digital sales, including proceeds from downloadable games, continued to surge. The popularity of “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie,” a 2026 animation film, also boosted its bottom line.

Companies like Nintendo tend to record their biggest sales during the present-giving Christmas and New Year’s seasons.

Nintendo did not break down quarterly details. It kept its projections for the full fiscal year through March 2027 unchanged at 310 billion yen profit, down nearly 27% from the previous fiscal year, on 2 trillion yen in sales, down 11%.

Like other technology companies, Nintendo is facing the problem of a computer chips crunch and surging prices due to the recent global boom in artificial intelligence.

Nintendo stocks rose 6.3% Thursday in Tokyo.

item.title: Lost in translation? Japanese minister blames X for diplomatic embarrassment
item.description:
TOKYO: A Japanese minister blamed Elon Musk’s X social media platform on Friday for almost plunging him into diplomatic hot water, after its automatic translation feature implied he did not know the names of world leaders he was meeting.

Trade Minister Ryosei Akazawa assured reporters that he knew the identity of the current prime minister of Bangladesh after a post with photos of the two included the name of ousted premier Sheikh Hasina in its translated version.

“This is actually a serious matter. It is possible that the Bangladeshi public might be left with the impression that, Japan’s Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry does not even know who our (Bangladeshi) prime minister is,” Akazawa told journalists.

His original Japanese-language post on X on Oct 28, accompanied by photos, stated that he met visiting Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

But the platform’s machine-translation tool incorrectly changed the English version to make Akazawa seem to declare that he met Sheikh Hasina, who has lived in exile in India since an uprising in 2024.

Making matters worse, it was not the first time Akazawa had fallen foul of a translation snafu on the platform.

He said a similar mistake occurred after he posted about his online meeting with Kuwait’s Oil Minister Tareq Al-Roumi on Thursday -- with the automatic translation feature saying he held talks with Qatar’s energy minister.

Akazawa added that his translated post on a meeting with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had also stated an incorrect name.

“I experienced this three times,” he said, appealing to X to fix the translation tool.

Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

item.title: Google turns off AI for schoolchildren by default
item.description:
Google has said it will switch off its AI tools for schoolchildren by default, after drawing criticism for pushing artificial intelligence features to students while schools are still debating how the technology should be used in classrooms.

The search engine juggernaut dominates technology in American schools. Its education apps, including Gmail, Docs and the Classroom platform, are used in classrooms across the country, and its low-cost Chromebook laptops are the devices US schools most often issue to students.

Under the changes Google announced in a blog post on Tuesday, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Search will be turned off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators switch them on.

Google told AFP the new controls would be rolled out worldwide, beginning in the United States, but that it had not yet set a date.

The changes also mean schools will not be able to give students Google Search without its AI features.

Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president for education, told The New York Times that “Search and A.I. are deeply integrated,” as AI features are now built into the company’s search engine.

If a school bans AI, he said, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google on X of “trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools.”

“No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children,” he wrote.

More than 150 million students worldwide use Google Classroom, according to a letter Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley sent to the company last month asking why AI features had been made the default on school devices.

In August, Google opened its Gemini chatbot in Classroom to students of all ages.

Students were shown starter prompts tied to their specific class and assignment, offering guided help or study guides, practice quizzes and flashcards built from their course materials.

The feature was switched on by default for students at schools that had already enabled Gemini.

New York and Los Angeles both announced plans in September to restrict access to AI tools on school devices.

“We are reviewing Google’s announcement and its potential implications for schools, educators and students,” a spokesperson for the Los Angeles Unified School District told AFP.

The spokesperson said the district believes AI can improve teaching and learning if it is introduced carefully and with clear safeguards, and pointed to district principles requiring that technology support rather than replace teachers and protect student privacy.

New York City Public Schools (NYCPS) are seeking more details from Google about the policy change, but the Gemini chatbot and AI mode are already disabled on Chromebooks used by students in NYC, a spokesperson for the district told AFP.

“NYCPS has also made requests to Google to disable the AI Overview displayed in the Google search result for students,” the spokesperson said.

In a statement on X, Google said Tuesday’s changes give “schools more choice, not less.”

“We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control,” Google said.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,276 as four die in 24 hours
item.description:
Four more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Friday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,276.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all four of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,171, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 105, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the four new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with four deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 1,239 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Friday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 236,714.
During the same period, 75 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 24,294.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 210,982 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 202,394 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.
